Got two links to recommend here. The first is connecting this to the other D&D skip SCP-1024 which actually does make the game come to life via supernatural means via a spellbook. Additionally the nod to MC&D can link to their hub. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

It is currently being investigated whether the effects of SCP-1974 are chemical, memetic, or supernatural.

To this:

It is currently being investigated whether the effects of SCP-1974 are chemical, memetic, or supernatural.

Changing this:

The Foundation takes no responsibility for the presence of hallucinogenic pens at the Marshall Carter & Dark auction on █/██/20██.

To this:

The Foundation takes no responsibility for the presence of hallucinogenic pens at the Marshall, Carter & Dark auction on █/██/20██.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Psychedelics are also referred to as "classical hallucinogens"- that is, the definitive hallucinogens of the sort that can make you see visions of the rainbow elf-people, as opposed to dissociatives that make you space out contemplating how cool your hands are, and deliriants that make you think the people in the TV want to steal your vital fluids.

LSD-25 is one of the standards by which other hallucinogens are defined, in other words.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: LSD-25 does not cause hallucinations. Psilocybin is a hallucinogen, but LSD-25 is purely a psychedelic lysergamide alkaloid.

item.content:encoded: I admit that is one reason I wrote this, and made it more of a deconstruction of "magic dice" rather than a straight version of them. One reason I think new folks like to try writing up dice is that there haven't been any dice SCPs around for a while, and it's harder now (with 1100+ SCPs on the site) to come up with an idea that isn't like something we already have. So, yeah, I'm hoping this means "Now there are dice on the site, so you don't have to write up more of them."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm not going to say you're wrong, since originally I had this up as a regular SCP. My rationale was that the technology is a bit off; I'm 99.9999% sure it's not actually possible to make one of these things, and have it work as described. But a bunch of folks commented it would be better as an -EX, I assume because the effects are completely explained by technology, and the tech doesn't sound all that futuristic.

It's in the grey area of sounding like a real thing someone could make, but it actually isn't.

+ If you really want to know why this thing is bogus, click here...
- OK, can we hide that, now that my suspension of disbelief is completely trashed?

OK, I assumed a ton of things are possible here, and most of them aren't:

  • Dr. Bright is correct that an audio transmitter probably won't fit into a normal-sized d20.
  • I don't think there is really an analog of DMSO that is solid at room temperature.
  • You probably can't mix DMSO with plastic and still have plastic.
  • Mixing DMSO with hallucinogens probably doesn't really work to make you trip via skin contact — although there are rumors to the contrary: Look up Lysergic Acid Crypto-Ethylene on the Web and decide for yourself.
  • Psychoacoustics seems to be a somewhat dodgy area of science and I'm pretty sure you can't hypnotize someone with some weird combination of sounds.
  • Even if all the stuff above worked, I don't think the effect would be that consistent.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's intentional: A -EX was a real SCP that was later found not to be anomalous. So: Incorrect information from the original SCP document is in strikethrough text, information that is still relevant in normal text, and corrections and added information after the item was found not to be anomalous are in italics. I know that isn't how the other -EX's were formatted, but I think this is easier to read/follow than the "complete strikethrough" version.

The dice are back, as a -EX. For those who have not read any -EX articles, this is an item once considered to be an SCP, but later explained as non-anomalous. The italic text indicates updated information.

I also took some advice from the comments and chat:

The dice don't blink.
There are no GOI's mentioned.
I added some examples of the effects.
I changed the hallucinogen to something a bit more unusual (thanks, ophite).
